about: The epistola of the formulary “7th Sunday after Pentecost” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: Brethren: I speak in human terms, on account of the infirmity of your flesh. For just as you presented your members to serve uncleanness and iniquity, leading to iniquity, so now present your members to serve justice, leading to sanctification. For when you were sin’s slaves, you were free from justice. What fruit, then, did you have at that time in the things that now make you blush? For their end is death. But now, freed from sin and made God’s slaves, you have your fruit leading to sanctification, and as its end, eternal life. For the wages of sin, death; but the grace of God, eternal life, in Christ Jesus our Lord.
